Re-energize the system by closing the supply breaker and restore the communications task logs after successful verification
Conduct final lockout release only after supervisory sign-off

data.body:
Hello Mesa Electrical Field Services,

Please carry out work order WO-1 on INV-2 (reseat_comms_card).

Steps, in order:
  1. Lockout and tagout breaker 52-In supplying power to INV-2 per NFPA 70E
  2. Verify zero energy at the inverter cabinet terminals using a calibrated multimeter
  3. Apply personal protective grounds on the breaker side as required by NFPA 70E
  4. Ensure trained personnel are standing by at the scene for emergency response
  5. Lockout and tagout the dedicated breaker supplying power to INV-2 per electrical safety procedures
  6. Verify zero energy at the inverter cabinet terminals using a calibrated multimeter
  7. Apply personal protective grounds on the breaker side as required by NFPA 70E
  8. Ensure trained personnel are standing by at the scene for emergency response
  9. De-isolate INV-2 from the grid and lock out/tag out the AC and DC disconnects
  10. Open the inverter cabinet and visually inspect the comms card for any signs of burns, loose harnesses, or corrosion
  11. Carefully unplug the fiber and Ethernet cables from the comms card, noting their positions
  12. Remove the communication card from its slot and reseat it firmly until it clicks into place
  13. Reconnect all fiber and Ethernet cables to their original ports on the reseated card
  14. Close the cabinet, restore AC and DC power, and power-cycle INV-2
  15. Ping the unit from SCADA to verify comms are restored and the display shows live data
  16. If the display remains dark or ping fails, re-open the cabinet and double-check all cable connections
  17. Log the repair and update the SCADA asset status to 'online'
  18. Remove personal protective grounds only after confirming safe conditions
  19. Re-energize the system by closing the supply breaker and restore the communications task logs after successful verification
  20. Conduct final lockout release only after supervisory sign-off
  21. Close the cabinet, restore AC and DC power, and power-cycle INV-2
  22. Ping the unit from SCADA to verify comms are restored and the display shows live data
  23. Remove personal protective grounds only after confirming safe conditions
  24. Re-energize the system by closing breaker 52-In supplying INV-2

Do not:
  - Do not attempt to power-cycle the unit before reseating the card, as this may mask a loose connection
  - Do not force the fiber cables; ensure ends are clean before reinsertion
  - Do not ignore a persistently dark display after reseating; further hardware replacement may be needed
  - Do not substitute an inspect-only visit or a power-cycle for the work order; it does not restore a failed comms card
  - Do not attempt to power-cycle the unit before reseating the card, as this may mask a loose connection.
  - Do not force the fiber cables; ensure ends are clean before reinsertion.
  - Do not ignore a persistently dark display after reseating; further hardware replacement may be needed.
  - Do not substitute an inspect-only visit or a power-cycle for the work order; it does not restore a failed comms card.

We will verify against the plant before closing this order:
  - INV-2 SCADA data_age_min at most 5 and status running
  - INV-2 answers comms_ping (its comms card is back on the network)
  - INV-2 display lit and showing readings in a camera view the verifier picks, not the contractor's photo
  - JEV verdict 'verified' from the registered camera stations and the sensor state

(Includes lessons from verified past incidents: L-demo-20261017-golden1.)

Reply to this email when the work is done.

GridTwin Ops (automated agent team)
